questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: To the lines $a x^2+2 h x y+b y^2=0$ the lines $a^2 x^2+2 h(a+b) x y+b^2 y^2=0$, are
questions.solution:
If the two pairs of straight lines have the same bisectors, then the two pairs are equally inclined.
The equation of the bisectors of the angle between the lines given by $a x^2+2 h x y+b y^2=0$ is
$\frac{x^2-y^2}{a-b}=\frac{x y}{h}...(i)$
The equation of the bisectors of the angle between the lines given by $a^2 x^2+2 h(a+b) x y+b^2 y^2=0 \text { is }\frac{x^2-y^2}{a^2-b^2}=\frac{x y}{h(a+b)}\Rightarrow \frac{x^2-y^2}{a-b}=\frac{x y}{h}...(ii)$
Clearly Eqs. (i) and (ii) are the same. The two pairs of straight lines are equally inclined.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The foci of the conic section $25 x^2+16 y^2-150 x=175$ are
questions.solution:
Given equation can be written as
$\frac{(x-3)^2}{16}+\frac{y^2}{25}=1\begin{aligned} & \text { Here, } a^2=16 \text { and } b^2=25 \\ & \therefore \quad \quad e=\sqrt{1-\frac{16}{25}}=\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}$
Hence, the foci of conic section are $(0, \pm b e)$ i.e. $(3, \pm 3)$.

questions.q:
If the angles between the pair of straight lines represented by the equation $x^2-3 x y+\lambda y^2+3 x-5 y+2=0$ is $\tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{3}$.
Where $\lambda$ is a non-negative real number, then $\lambda$ is
questions.solution:
Let $\theta$ be the angle between the given pair of straight lines
$x^2-3 x y+\lambda y^2+3 x-5 y+2=0$  ...(i)
$\therefore \quad \theta=\tan ^{-1} \frac{1}{3} \quad$ (given) or $\quad \tan \theta=\frac{1}{3}$
We know that,
$\tan \theta=\frac{2 \sqrt{h^2-a b}}{a+b}$  ...(ii)
where, $\quad h=-\frac{3}{2}, a=1, b=\lambda$
put these value in Eq. (ii), we get
$\begin{aligned}
\frac{1}{3} & =\frac{2 \sqrt{\frac{9}{4}-\lambda \cdot 1}}{1+\lambda} \\
\Rightarrow \quad(1+\lambda) & =3 \sqrt{9-4 \lambda}
\end{aligned}$
On squaring both sides, we get
$\begin{aligned}(1+\lambda)^2 & =(3 \sqrt{9-4 \lambda})^2 \\ 1+\lambda^2+2 \lambda & =81-36 \lambda\end{aligned}\begin{array}{rr}
\Rightarrow & \lambda^2+38 \lambda-80=0 \\
\Rightarrow & \lambda^2+40 \lambda-2 \lambda-80=0 \\
\Rightarrow & \lambda(\lambda+40)-2(\lambda+40)=0 \\
\Rightarrow & (\lambda-2)(\lambda+40)=0 \\
\Rightarrow & \lambda=2,-40 \Rightarrow \lambda=2
\end{array}$
( $\because^{\prime} \lambda$ ' is non-negative real number)

questions.q: The circumcentre of a triangle formed by the lines $x y+2 x+2 y+4=0$ and $x+y+2=0$, is
questions.solution:
Given lines are $x y+2 x+2 y+4=0$...(i) and $\quad x+y+2=0$...(ii)

From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get $x y=0\Rightarrow \quad x=y=0\therefore$ Vertices of triangle are $(-2,0),(0,0),(0,-2)$ In a right angled triangle circumcentre is the mid-point of hypotenuse. $\therefore$ Point $(-1,-1)$ is the required coordinate of the circumcentre.
